title: White House announces removal of over 760,000 Obamacare enrollees
seoTitle: White House Removes 760K+ Obamacare Enrollees for Fraud
subtitle: Vice President JD Vance and Administrator Mehmet Oz explain the crackdown on ACA fraud
excerpt: The U.S. government will remove over 760,000 people from Obamacare, citing fraud and phantom enrollees, and impose re-verification on 419,000.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The announcement regarding the removal of over 760,000 Obamacare enrollees was made during a U.S. government press conference, where Vice President JD Vance and CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz pointed to widespread fraud within the program.

Reason for removing enrollees

According to Vance, the measure aims to save $2.2 billion in improperly paid federal subsidies. Oz added that some of the enrollees were “phantom enrollees”—people who do not exist—and that others may have been signed up without their knowledge.

Additional verification for 419,000 applicants

In addition to the removals, 419,000 individuals will undergo re-verification to confirm income, legal residency, and the presence of a Social Security number, a requirement that will become mandatory for all future applicants.

Broker suspensions and moratorium

The administration also suspended brokers and agents involved in improper enrollments and enacted a six-month moratorium on new brokers or agents, a measure that adds to the suspension of hundreds of professionals carried out by the Biden administration in 2024.

Political context of the initiative

Republicans present the action as a crackdown on fraud in healthcare programs ahead of the November midterm elections, while critics claim the measure could leave many people without coverage. Brad Woodhouse, chair of Protect Our Care, described the task force as “a political stunt designed to throw even more people off their coverage while pretending to save taxpayers’ money.”

Impact on coverage numbers

Recent data from the Department of Health and Human Services indicate that 19.2 million people were enrolled in the ACA in February, down from 21.8 million during the same period the previous year. Rising health insurance rates for Obamacare, employer coverage, and Medicare in 2026 were also highlighted as a concern for the public.

With information from CNN.
